cards.text: This is a song of David, Israel's king, written for the choirmaster. No warm-up, no small talk, no "how's everybody doing tonight." First line: "Save me, O God, for the waters are up to my neck."

cards.question: David is sinking into the miry depths. He says that down there, there's no ___.

cards.text: David has cried out so long that he's worn out and his throat is parched. His eyes fail from looking for his God.
And the water isn't his only problem: the people who hate him outnumber the hairs of his head. Friend, that's not a few haters, that's a SOLD-OUT STADIUM.

cards.question: David says the people who hate him have a good reason for it.
David says he didn't steal anything, but he still has to ___.

cards.text: But David doesn't claim he's perfect. He tells God, "You know my folly, O God, and my guilt is not hidden from You."

cards.question: David knows his own folly. What does he ask God about the people who hope in Him?

answers.text: That they not be ashamed through him
That they come and rescue him

cards.text: David says he's endured scorn for God's sake, and even his own brothers treat him like a stranger. That's the family group chat going dead quiet every time he hits send.

cards.question: David says something has consumed him, and it's why his brothers treat him like a stranger. What is it?
David says the insults of people who insult God have fallen on him.

cards.text: David says he wept and fasted. He even made sackcloth his clothing.

cards.question: When David weeps, fasts and wears sackcloth, people respect him for it.

cards.text: It gets worse: the folks who sit at the gate mock him, and he's the song of drunkards. Friend, when they've written a SONG about you, you are having a ROUGH stretch.

cards.question: Mocked at the gate and turned into a song, what does David do next?
David asks God to answer him. What is he counting on?

cards.text: Then David's right back in the water. Pull me out of the mire, he prays, don't let the depths swallow me, and don't let the Pit close its mouth over me.

cards.question: David tells God to take all the time He needs to answer.
David is in distress with foes all around. What does he ask God to do for his soul?

cards.text: David reminds God that He knows all of it: his reproach, his shame and his disgrace. Every one of David's adversaries is right there before God.

cards.question: Insults have broken David's heart. He looked for comforters, but he found ___.

cards.text: And his enemies aren't done. They poisoned his food with gall.

cards.question: David's throat is parched. What do his enemies give him to quench his thirst?

cards.text: Now David prays about his enemies, and he does not hold back. He asks God to make their table a snare and to pour out His wrath on them.

cards.question: What reason does David give for praying this way about his enemies?

answers.text: They persecute the one God struck

cards.text: He goes further still. He asks that they be blotted out of the Book of Life and not listed with the righteous.

cards.question: After praying about his enemies, David says he's feeling fine now.

cards.text: Up to his NECK, mocked at the gate, and David says, "I will praise God’s name in song and exalt Him with thanksgiving." They turned him into a song, and now he's got one of his own.

cards.question: David says his song of praise will please the LORD more than something else. What is it?

cards.text: Not just any bull, friend, a bull with horns AND hooves, the full deluxe model, and the praise still wins. And David says the humble will see it and rejoice.

cards.question: David says the LORD despises His captive people.

cards.text: Then David calls on heaven and earth to praise Him. The seas too, and everything that moves in them.

cards.question: David says God will save Zion and ___ the cities of Judah.
Who does David say will settle in those cities?

findings.problem: The card says David 'asks God to make their table a snare.' Psalm 69:22 is a wish, 'May their table become a snare,' and it does not name who it is spoken to. Only verse 24 ('Pour out Your wrath') is addressed to God. Turning the 'May' line into a request made to God adds an addressee and changes what the text calls the line, like the Naomi example. Something like 'He says, May their table become a snare, and he asks God to pour out His wrath on them' would keep it true.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: The right answer, 'They persecute the one God struck,' sounds like Bible wording and is the only answer that involves God. The wrong answers, 'They burned down his house' and 'They stole his family's land,' are plain everyday grievances. The right answer stands out by tone. No earlier card mentions God striking anyone, so a baker would pick it for how it sounds, not by reasoning it out. The wrong answers should match it in tone, for example by also describing what the enemies do to people God has dealt with or wounded.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
